retention.title: Complete-case selection changes the diagnosis mix
retention.alt: Complete records were retained in 17.2% of CKD and 76.7% of non-CKD patients. Median creatinine changed by -0.20 mg/dL overall and +1.85 within CKD. The reweighted complete-case median was 2.20 mg/dL.
retention.caption: A shows complete records divided by all records in each diagnosis and Wilson 95% intervals. B compares the complete-case median with the median among patients with a creatinine measurement. Bars are pointwise 95% percentile intervals from a patient bootstrap stratified by diagnosis, using the same draws for both views. The three pooled medians examine how much the diagnosis mix alone changes the result.

distributions.title: Five clinical measurements across three data views
distributions.alt: Five empirical distribution plots compare available, complete and imputed measurements. Hemoglobin has a visible imputation step because 52 missing values receive 12.65. Creatinine and blood urea show long right tails.
distributions.caption: Each panel plots a right-continuous empirical cumulative distribution in the three views, using all observed values in that view as its denominator. Counts follow legend order. Creatinine and blood urea use base-10 axes with native-unit labels; all values were positive and the full ranges are shown. Hemoglobin uses the UCI source unit, recorded as g.

renal_association.title: Creatinine and urea under different missing-data rules
renal_association.alt: 380 paired measurements show a long upper tail, including row 22 at creatinine 76 and urea 180 mg/dL. After complete-case selection, Pearson r changes by +0.31 and Spearman rho by -0.23.
renal_association.caption: A shows every jointly observed pair with no jitter or exclusions. Axes use base-10 scales and native-unit tick labels; coincident records can overlap. B displays native-unit coefficients with pointwise bootstrap 95% intervals for observed and complete pairs. The single-imputed estimates are descriptive, with no uncertainty bars. C shows pointwise 95% percentile intervals for complete-minus-available changes, resampling patients within diagnosis and applying both rules to each bootstrap draw.

pca.title: Standardization changes the first principal component
pca.alt: PC1 explains 68.8% of variance in original units and 43.3% after standardization. Random blood glucose dominates the original-unit axis; urea, hemoglobin and creatinine have the largest absolute standardized coefficients.
pca.caption: A shows signed unit-length PC1 eigenvector coordinates (a whole eigenvector can be sign-flipped). B gives the fraction of within-fit variance explained by each component. Both fits center their five columns. Standardization additionally divides by the population standard deviation (ddof=0).

imputation_validation.title: How far does a median fill miss a held-out value?
imputation_validation.alt: Five rows contrast diagnosis-specific signed validation errors on a common training-IQR scale and mean absolute errors in original units. For creatinine, the median standardized signed error is -0.51 in CKD and +0.20 in non-CKD.
imputation_validation.caption: Five-fold validation masks observed entries. A uses the held-out prediction minus the measured value, divided by the training interquartile range in that fold, then takes the diagnosis-specific median. B gives mean absolute error in original units. The plotted point estimates describe measured records. Missing records have no observed target for validating their imputed value.
